document_summary: California Civil Code § 1950.5, the statewide statute governing residential security deposits (amount caps, inspections, photographs, itemized statements and return), as amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security (any deposit, fee or advance charge) above one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. A narrower class of small landlords is capped at two months' rent, and the two-month cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. The two-month cap applies only if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer; mutually agreed paid alterations requested by the tenant; the cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. Service members cannot be charged the 2-month small-landlord amount; higher-than-standard security for service members due to credit etc. must be explained in writing and the excess returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date inferred from subdivision (c)(6), which says the subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. Section last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective 2026-01-01; service member provisions effective on or after 2025-04-01.  Return/itemization, photograph and nonrefundable rules are in separate records.  The cap amount itself was not changed by the amendment.  Medium-high confidence in date since it is inferred. rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Return of deposit and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any deductions and return any remaining security. Deductions are limited to amounts reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and cleaning to the move-in condition, and copies of invoices or receipts are required unless deductions total $125 or less or the tenant waived the right.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential security for a rental agreement for property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Documentation requirements do not apply if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived them; good-faith estimates are allowed where repairs or documents cannot be completed within 21 days, with completion within 14 days.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date null: the document does not state when the 21-day requirement originally took effect (only the 2026-01-01 effective date of the latest amendment, AB 414, which added electronic-return and multiple-tenant provisions). Bad-faith failure to comply forfeits the landlord's claim to the security and may bring statutory damages up to twice the deposit (subd. (h)(7), (m)).

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Landlord photograph requirements
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit at or immediately before the start of the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit after possession is returned and after any repairs or cleanings, and provide those photographs with the itemized statement when deductions are made.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies where security is held; move-in photographs apply to tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – No 'nonrefundable' deposits
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as nonrefundable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date null: the document does not state when this subdivision first took effect.
